programme.title: The Many Faces of Alison Steadman
programme.desc: Alison Steadman talks about her impressive career, featuring archive footage and testimony from friends and colleagues. The programme progresses from her earliest appearances on screen, to what drove her choices, for good or ill, and their consequences. Contains footage and stills from programmes such as `Gavin and Stacey', `Abigail's Party', `Newshounds', `Nuts in May' and her early appearances in `Frost'.

programme.title: Alison Steadman Remembers... Girl
programme.desc: National treasure Alison Steadman tells the story of one of the most groundbreaking and yet also most overlooked moments in British television. Despite the popular perception that Channel 4's Brookside broadcast TV's first lesbian kiss in 1994, in reality it was Alison and Myra Frances who first broke the taboo, 20 years earlier in the 1974 drama Girl.

programme.title: Gateways Grind: London's Secret Lesbian Club
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig goes behind the iconic green door of one of the most famous lesbian venues in the world, The Gateways Club in London. Starting off as a meeting place for bohemians, it became lesbian-only under the watchful management of the enigmatic Gina Ware and her sidekick Smithy until its closure in 1985. The Gates' former clientele recount the many stories of love, heartbreak, friendship, scandal and sanctuary that played out in the club, including the venue's appearance in a Hollywood film.

programme.title: Dame Maggie Smith - A Celebration
programme.desc: A special tribute to the celebrated and enigmatic actress Dame Maggie Smith, who remains a mystery to her friends and perhaps also to herself - hear the story of her remarkable life told by those who knew her best as they celebrate her much-loved appearances across film and TV spanning almost 70 years. Maggie, who passed away in September 2024, is beloved the world over for her countless iconic screen performances - in recent years she gained a new level of popularity playing the razor-tongued Lady Violet Crawley in Downton Abbey, but Maggie remained a very private person who had little time for the trappings that came with fame in spite of her success. Using Maggie's own voice as its heartbeat - and featuring personal accounts from close friends and colleagues from across her career - the film tells the story of a girl born in pre-war Essex who took Broadway and the West End by storm against the odds before eventually becoming one of the nation's most popular and respected performers.
